summary: Jerseyman Island light at the north-west entrance to Arichat Harbour, Isle Madame, has shown a red light since 1872; its tower was replaced in 1950 and again in 2017.

structures.note: Built with an attached dwelling by F. S. Cunningham for $1,200 (Lighthouse Friends).

Replaced the 1872 tower and dwelling. Lighthouse Friends calls the tower wooden; the Preservation Society's light table gives 'Tapered square wood tower' and dates the replacement 1953 (its narrative says 1950).

structures.type: square tower, white with a red upper portion
structures.note: Modular, aluminum-framed replacement (Isle Madame Lighthouses); Lighthouse Friends describes four sections lifted in by helicopter.

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (Lighthouse Friends). Lighthouse Friends says the light is best seen by boat, or from the eastern end of Veterans Memorial Drive in Arichat. The Preservation Society gives site access as 'By Boat'.

events.note: Lit 10 July 1872 (Department notice, as Lighthouse Friends prints it).
Tower and attached dwelling built by F. S. Cunningham for $1,200.
Storm damage; cable stays and cribwork were added to the tower afterwards.
Hand foghorn given to the keeper, George Vigneau.
Seventh-order dioptric lens replaced the catoptric lamps and reflectors.
New tower and detached keeper's house replaced the 1872 station.
Battery-operated foghorn running around the clock.
Submarine cable from the mainland brought commercial power.
Station de-staffed; boathouse converted to an engine room for a diesel generator.
Keeper's dwelling removed from the island; later floated to Arichat.
1950 tower replaced by a modular tower in September 2017.
Preservation Society's light table dates the replacement tower to 1953; its narrative, Lighthouse Friends and Isle Madame Lighthouses say 1950.
Preservation Society's light table gives 1922 for the seventh-order dioptric lens; the Department's 1902 report and Lighthouse Friends give 1902.

corrections.why: The tower standing since September 2017 is a modular, aluminum-framed replacement (Isle Madame Lighthouses). The wooden 1872 tower was removed in 2017 (Lighthouse Friends, Isle Madame Lighthouses).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Lighthouse Friends and the Department's report for the year ended 30 June 1902 agree on 1902 (the 1901 report had said the lens was ordered from England). The Preservation Society's light table gives 1922 for the seventh-order lens; the Department's 1902 report dates it earlier. The story states both.

notes_for_editor: Checked 2026-10-28 against the sources and page images. Two Department keeper rows were matched by position in the OCR and were checked on the page images: 1904 table (1905 report, scan 176, printed p.163): Vigneau, George on the Jerseyman Island row; 1911 table (1912 report, scan 244, printed p.237): Alphonse Theriault on the Jerseyman Island row. The Commissioner's 1902 and 1903 reports (scans 46 and 89) quote correctly. Open disagreements, stated in the story: (a) naming: the Preservation Society and the Dorey essay credit the Robin family (Dorey: John and Charles Robin named it after discovering the harbour in 1764); Lighthouse Friends and Isle Madame Lighthouses credit Jersey traders. (b) Irving R. Latimer's appointment: the memoir has the family landing on 1 April 1930; Lighthouse Friends and Isle Madame Lighthouses give 1931. (c) 2017 tower: Lighthouse Friends says it toppled in August; Isle Madame Lighthouses says it was demolished in early summer. (d) Replacement tower: 1950 in the Preservation Society's narrative, Lighthouse Friends and Isle Madame; 1953 in the Preservation Society's light table. (e) Seventh-order lens: 1902 in the Department's report and Lighthouse Friends; 1922 in the Preservation Society's light table. (f) Site position: Lighthouse Friends puts the light on the northern tip of the third of three islands; the Preservation Society puts it at the north end of West Jerseyman Island. (g) The raid: Dorey dates it September 1776; Lighthouse Friends gives no date. (h) The Preservation Society's light table gives 'Site Access: By Boat'; the record's visit.boat_only is now supported. (i) Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights gives 'Seasonal' operation and 'Flash 1 s; eclipse 3 s'. (j) Russ Latimer is a living author: only the memoir's house, pay and arrival details are used, with no personal detail beyond what the memoir prints. (k) Lighthouse Friends and Preservation Society text is copyrighted: the story uses facts and short phrases only. (l) The 1872 Department notice is read through Lighthouse Friends; the 1872 report is not in the corpus. (m) Isle Madame Lighthouses gives 'Georges' Vigneau and 'Joseph Martell Jan. 1931 - March 1931'; the story says 'early in 1931'. (n) Lighthouse Friends' own text quotes the memoir as 1930 while its keeper list gives 1931.
